narrative: Distilled 2026-08-29 from a reference the platform owner brought (thepottershouse.org) as the worked example of the ARENA language. A multi-campus church of several thousand with a conference, a school and a weekly broadcast; the communications director opens with the vision, speaks in short declarative lines, has a wordmark everyone knows and a calendar that never stops. Fills library holes: energizing at institutional scale, curious + ambitious visitors, established_attached on a large organisation, moment_of_need + steady_rhythm, grotesque_bold display, and dense_intentional on a centred dark page. Resulting direction: A HOUSE THAT SPEAKS IN CAPITALS — a near-black page with one light-grey photo panel per screen, a wide heavy uppercase display with a ghost watermark word behind every section title, one orange for links and the one highlight, square everything, diagonal seams, an info bar of service times under the hero and events three-up. Teaches: the watermark title, two-ground rhythm, diagonal seams, ghost-outline buttons, and the calendar as the page's heartbeat.

palette.because: Two grounds only — a near-black page and one light-grey photo panel per screen (P4: the house performs); the wordmark's orange is the one warm colour, spent on links and a single highlight, never a filled button (P3, P16).

typography.pairing_logic: A wide, heavy uppercase grotesque at monumental scale for every title, with a ghost watermark of the section's category word behind it in the ground one step lighter; a plain Helvetica-class body. Maximum formal contrast (P5, expert_above) — the house speaks in capitals, the body speaks plainly.
typography.because: Declarative lines at banner scale ARE the voice; the watermark makes every section its own arena.

layout.because: P6: symmetry implies verdict — the name centred over the photo panel; P7: a mixed audience gets the calendar dense on screen two (events three-up, times in an info bar) because the schedule is the product.

motion.signature_move: the diagonal cut — each section's seam slides into place as it arrives, the one shape the page repeats
motion.because: P8: one move that restates the house's geometry; the calendar and the photos hold still.

hero_concept.concept_statement: THE NAME in wide heavy capitals across a light-grey photo panel, two ghost-outlined uppercase buttons beneath — WATCH NOW → and PLAN YOUR VISIT — then the panel's bottom edge cut on a diagonal into the black, and an info bar: SUNDAYS 9 AM · the address · the broadcast.
hero_concept.because: vision_first + energizing at institutional scale → the name is the statement, and the service times are the first thing under it (moment_of_need: 'this Sunday').

whitespace.because: A house with something on every night is dense on purpose — sections are separated by diagonals and ground changes, not by air.

notes: every banner-sized sentence in their copy becomes a section title in wide capitals with its category word ghosted behind it (ABOUT US behind WHO WE ARE, EVENTS behind WHAT'S HAPPENING)
events sit in a three-up card row with square corners and the date in orange
the give and watch buttons are ghost outlines in uppercase — orange is for links only
stats are gatherings, campuses, years — stated flat in the body face, no monuments
voice_to_visual.because: A voice of declarative lines becomes a page of titled arenas; the calendar carries the energy the copy promises.

rule_break.what: every section title has its own category word printed behind it as a ghost watermark — a second, larger headline the reader is not meant to read
rule_break.because: The watermark is the house's scale made visible; it is the one ornament on an otherwise square, plain page.

tension.pole_a: a house that speaks in capitals
tension.pole_b: a place for one person this Sunday
tension.expression: The capitals own the titles, the watermarks, the grey panels and the diagonals; the one person owns the info bar, the 'there's a place for you' card in orange link text and the plan-your-visit ghost button.
tension.because: All scale reads as a broadcast; all welcome reads as a small church — the house is both.

first_impression.feel_in_3s: Something big is happening here, and it's this Sunday.
first_impression.remember: The name in wide capitals over the grey panel, and the times right under it.
first_impression.because: energizing for the curious = scale and a concrete next step in the same screen.

language.because: A large house with an attached wordmark, bold conviction, an event calendar and a modern declarative voice — one voice, one warm colour, the calendar as the heartbeat; Hearth would be too small and soft for several thousand people.

distinctiveness_check.notes: Shares the dark single-accent typographic hero with e6 and the dense single-accent typographic hero with e8, but is centred and wide-grotesque with a warm accent where e6 is asymmetric and expressive; the only grotesque_bold display and the only two-ground diagonal rhythm in the library.

banned_defaults_avoided: no hero video with dimmed overlay

summary_for_practitioner: Your site speaks in capitals. Your name runs in wide, heavy letters across a light-grey photo panel, with WATCH NOW and PLAN YOUR VISIT as outlined buttons under it, and the panel cuts away on a diagonal into black with your service times right there in a bar. Every section title has its own bigger, ghosted word behind it — ABOUT US behind WHO WE ARE — and everything is square-cornered. Your one colour is the orange from your wordmark, used only for links and dates. Events sit three across with the date in orange; your numbers are stated plainly in the body text, never as monuments.
